title: History of the Clever Youth and the Miserly Baker

full_text:
During a dry summer in Damascus when wheat was scarce, a wealthy baker named Kasim locked three large storage bins of flour in his cellar, refusing to bake until bread prices doubled in the bazaar. Poor mothers stood weeping outside his shuttered shop while he claimed he had no flour left.

A resourceful young apprentice named Bilal resolved to break the artificial famine.
He knew that Kasim was pathologically fearful of rats eating his hoarded grain. Bilal bought a large clay pot containing twenty fat, noisy crickets, walked to Kasim's back cellar window at night, and emptied the crickets through the iron grate into the dark flour bins.

The crickets began chirping loudly, scratching frantically against the wooden partitions and dry wheat husks.
Inside his house, Kasim heard the rhythmic scratching and rustling. He panicked:
'Heavens! Thousands of giant granary rats have invaded my flour! If they soil the grain, my entire fortune is lost!'

Kasim rushed into the street in his nightshirt, shouting:
'Help! Porters, neighbors! My granary is overrun by ravenous rats! I will sell every sack of flour for half-price right now to anyone who carries it away before morning!'

Bilal, waiting in the lane with fifty townspeople and porters, cheered:
'We are ready, Master Baker!'
The townsfolk carried out every single sack of flour, paying Kasim half-price in cash. When the bins were emptied, they found not a single rat, only twenty harmless chirping crickets!

Kasim realized he had been completely outwitted, but with his sacks sold and the cash in hand, he could not retract the sale.
The bread was baked, the prices returned to normal, and the children of Damascus were fed, proving that compassionate wit can defeat cold-hearted avarice.
moral: Hoarding food during famine to artificially inflate prices is a grave sin that invites swift, poetic retribution.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "History of the Third Larrikin"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
